cells.tense: You are reading the shape underneath the detail right now, and it is not costing you the detail.
cells.ask: Say which pattern you have chosen, out loud, once, then let someone else use it badly without correcting them.
cells.core:
You can look at a pile of detail and see what it is actually doing. Not the story about it, not who said what — the structure underneath. That is rarer than it sounds, and it usually stays invisible to whoever has it.
What makes it hold is that the reading comes out of real contact with the material. You are not theorizing over the top of it; you are close enough to the thing that the shape shows itself. So the pattern you name tends to be one other people can actually use. What comes next is not more of it. It is letting the thing you understood leave your hands and go do its work.
cells.sheetLine: You see the shape underneath, and you have earned the right to.
cells.verb: Seeing the pattern underneath the thing
cells.place: At the point of choosing this one and not that one

cells.tense: You are bracing for a moment that has not arrived yet, reading the shape of it ahead of time.
cells.ask: Pick the version you have now and act on it today, then leave the rest alone until something real comes back.
cells.core:
You are running the pattern ahead of schedule. Sitting with anything, you have already worked out what it will do and who is doing what to whom — and the reading keeps needing another pass. The analysis has stopped producing clarity and started producing more analysis.
The alertness is real; you are good at seeing mechanism. But right now it feeds on imagining rather than on contact, so it just grows. You cannot think your way out of thinking too much — the exit is doing something before you have finished understanding it. One small thing, chosen and moved on, gives your mind something solid to work with.
What this costs to keep: the more of the future gets worked out in advance, the less any of it can surprise you into anything useful.
cells.sheetLine: You are working out the room before you enter it, again and again.

cells.tense: You are still standing at a door you decided against, treating the plain surface as all there is.
cells.ask: Take something you work with closely and explain what it means, not just how it works, to someone who will ask you why.
cells.core:
You are taking things at face value on purpose. What you can see and touch and state plainly is what you work with, and anything under it — symbol, meaning, the shape a thing makes — stays out of reach because reaching for it has not worked for you.
No reading of what happened before this. What is visible now: you direct yourself competently at the surface and the depth does not get used, so your grasp of things stays useful but thin. The ability is there; it has just been running on nothing.
The way back is not straining to see deeper. It is handing something you work with to someone else — explaining what it means, and answering when they push. The depth gets pulled through the act of passing something on.
cells.sheetLine: You take things at face value, and the meaning stays unused.

cells.tense: You are setting the direction with full attention while calling the direction something that just happened to you.
cells.ask: Name the pattern you are currently living inside, out loud to one person, and say what you put there and why.
cells.core:
There is a shape running your decisions right now, and you are inside it rather than looking at it. It feels like the way things are — the sensible path, the obvious call — and you would not describe it as chosen.
No claim about where the shape came from or who taught it to you. What is factual is that you keep steering by it, and the steering does not get counted as yours. The pattern is doing real work in your life, and you would not say so out loud were you asked.
The way forward is smaller than insight. Say the pattern to one person and connect it to a choice you actually made. That is the part that turns a shape you live inside into one you live by.
cells.sheetLine: The pattern is steering, and you call it the way things are.
cells.verb: Seeing the pattern underneath the thing
